explanations.explanation_trachea: The trachea (windpipe) carries air between the larynx and the lungs. C-shaped rings of cartilage hold it open.
explanations.explanation_bronchi: The trachea divides into the left and right bronchi, which branch again and again into bronchioles that end in tiny air sacs called alveoli.
explanations.explanation_right_upper_lobe: The right lung has three lobes. The upper lobe is separated from the middle lobe by the horizontal fissure.
explanations.explanation_right_middle_lobe: The middle lobe is found only in the right lung, between the horizontal and oblique fissures.
explanations.explanation_right_lower_lobe: The lower lobes rest on the diaphragm. The oblique fissure separates them from the lobes above.
explanations.explanation_left_upper_lobe: The left lung has only two lobes, leaving room for the heart. The cardiac notch is cut into its front edge.
explanations.explanation_left_lower_lobe: In the alveoli of every lobe, oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out to be breathed away.
explanations.explanation_diaphragm: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped sheet of muscle under the lungs. When it contracts and flattens, air is drawn into the lungs.
